title: good first issue: add a minimal end-to-end example to examples/
body:
## What

Add a new file `examples/quickstart.py` that walks a new user through the basic lifecycle in under 30 lines:

1. `Alethech.init()` — generate keypair + genesis commit
2. `alethech.commit(...)` — add 2-3 commits with different types (semantic, episodic, procedural)
3. `alethech.verify()` — verify the store
4. `alethech.rotate_keys()` — rotate keys
5. `alethech.verify()` — verify again (should still pass — reachability guarantee)
6. `alethech.export()` — export the store
7. Print a clean summary at each step

## Why

The README has code snippets but no single runnable file. A new user who `pip install alethech`s needs to see the full lifecycle in one place to "get it". The `examples/` directory currently has more advanced demos (cross-language transfer, langchain integration) but no "hello world".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `examples/quickstart.py` exists, runs with `python examples/quickstart.py` after `pip install alethech`
- [ ] No external dependencies beyond `alethech` itself
- [ ] Output is human-readable, each step labeled
- [ ] Total runtime < 5 seconds
- [ ] Code is commented (each step explains what it demonstrates)
- [ ] File ends with a comment pointing to the next example to look at

## How to run it locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/eddyflores100-lang/alethech.git
cd alethech
pip install -e .
python examples/quickstart.py
```

## Difficulty

Beginner-friendly. No cryptography knowledge needed — just call the public API in order. If any API call feels awkward or undocumented, that's feedback worth surfacing in the PR.

## What you'll learn

- The basic shape of the alethech API
- The lifecycle: init → commit → verify → rotate → verify → export
- How key rotation preserves historical verifiability (the reachability guarantee)

## Mentoring

I'll review PRs within 24 hours. If you get stuck on API design (not a bug), open a draft PR with your question as a comment and tag me.
